# SWARM (SWM)

> SWARM (ticker SWM) is a privacy coin: a cryptocurrency with its own proof-of-work blockchain, on which payments can be shielded so that sender, receiver and amount stay encrypted on-chain. Its supply is capped at 20,999,987.3152 SWM. Its mainnet has been live since 2 October 2026; until 31 October 2026, 15:42 UTC only the project’s own machines mine, for the next 24 hours the people on its waiting list can mine too, and from 1 November 2026, 15:42 UTC mining is open to everyone.

Source: https://swarm.green/what-is-swarm and the pages linked below. Published by the SWARM project. Fixed rules and published facts only; for live figures read https://swarm.green/data/status.json or the block explorer at https://mainnet.explore.swarm.green.

## How SWARM keeps a payment private

SWARM has two kinds of payment. A **shielded** payment uses zero-knowledge proofs: the chain records that a valid payment happened without recording who paid whom or how much, so sender, receiver and amount stay encrypted on-chain. A **transparent** payment is public, as on most blockchains.

SWARM Wallet gives you a shielded address by default and tells you which kind of payment you are about to make. Shielding protects what is written to the chain. It does not protect everything about how you use the network: your own network connection, for example, is a separate matter.

## How SWM is issued

SWM is issued only by mining. A block is found about every 75 seconds and pays 6.25 SWM; the reward halves every 1,680,000 blocks, about every 4 years, so the supply approaches 20,999,987.3152 SWM and never exceeds it. The genesis block holds no spendable coins. The first 30 days are a closed start. Until 31 October 2026, 15:42 UTC only the project's own machines can mine: in those 29 days about 33,408 blocks are produced, about 208,800 SWM (80% to the project's mining wallet, 20% to the three funds), about 0.99% of the cap. From then until 1 November 2026, 15:42 UTC the people on the waiting list can mine too; from that moment mining is open to everyone and the node software will be published on this site. Why: the infrastructure around the coin, liquidity pools included, needs coins before public mining begins; the aim is an orderly, predictable start.

Every block reward is split the same way for the whole schedule: 80% to the miner who found the block and 20% to three published project addresses (8% Core Development, 4% Grants & Ecosystem and 8% Community & Development Reserve). Those shares are paid block by block, in public, and the percentages cannot be changed. The full schedule is on the [network page](https://swarm.green/network); the three addresses and how their keys are held are on the [verify page](https://swarm.green/verify).

## Proof of work

SWARM is secured by proof of work, Equihash 200,9, left unchanged from the open-source code it builds on. Specialised hardware for this proof of work exists and nothing in the rules keeps larger miners out.

## What it is built on

SWARM is built on proven, open-source code that has secured real money for years. The consensus rules and the cryptography are left unmodified; SWARM adds its own network, its economics and its apps. The code is public at [github.com/Swarmcoin/swarm-releases](https://github.com/Swarmcoin/swarm-releases): read it, build it, check it.

## The software

Everything you need is published with its SHA-256 checksum in the [Ecosystem](https://swarm.green/ecosystem): [SWARM Wallet](https://swarm.green/ecosystem/wallet) (Windows, macOS and Linux; also as a hosted web wallet at wallet.swarm.green, held by the SWARM server), [SWARM Messenger](https://swarm.green/ecosystem/messenger) (Windows, macOS and Linux) and [SWARM Browser](https://swarm.green/ecosystem/browser) (Windows). The mainnet block explorer is at [mainnet.explore.swarm.green](https://mainnet.explore.swarm.green). The [roadmap](https://swarm.green/roadmap) separates what is live from what is only planned.

## Emission schedule

An era is the stretch between two halvings. Later eras continue the same halving.

| Era | Block heights | Block reward (SWM) | Issued in era (SWM) | Cumulative supply (SWM) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 1 – 1,679,998 | 6.25 | 10,499,987.5 | 10,499,987.5 |
| 1 | 1,679,999 – 3,359,998 | 3.125 | 5,250,000 | 15,749,987.5 |
| 2 | 3,359,999 – 5,039,998 | 1.5625 | 2,625,000 | 18,374,987.5 |
| 3 | 5,039,999 – 6,719,998 | 0.7812 | 1,312,500 | 19,687,487.5 |
| 4 | 6,719,999 – 8,399,998 | 0.3906 | 656,250 | 20,343,737.5 |

Mining rewards mature after 100 blocks before they can be spent.

## Block reward split

The whole emission schedule. Every halving reduces all four amounts proportionally, keeping the same 80 / 8 / 4 / 8 structure, until block rewards reach zero. Each allocation is paid automatically to its predefined destination address. Destinations can only be changed through a formal protocol upgrade; the percentages themselves cannot be changed.

| Recipient | Share | Per block in era 0 (SWM) | Published address |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Miner | 80% | 5 | the address the miner chose |
| Core Development | 8% | 0.5 | `s3fLmEHc1xqs8KAe7QS7oupkhuGDjidV4eq` |
| Grants & Ecosystem | 4% | 0.25 | `s3RiGvK5JzS8eh6ywN3K22f2LzDAhicgFuq` |
| Community & Development Reserve | 8% | 0.5 | `s3g3pzQVhvVX17bzrrEN3vmcXZWSpj7KFVp` |

Custody of the three project addresses: Pay-to-script-hash, 2-of-3 multisig (s3…). Each script is controlled by three key shares generated offline at the launch key ceremony and held under the custody policy published with the launch manifest; two of the three are needed to spend.

## Network endpoints

- Light-wallet server (TLS): `lwd-main.swarm.green:443`
- Block explorer: https://mainnet.explore.swarm.green
- Network name: `SwarmMainnet`; light-wallet chain label: `swarm-mainnet`

## Address formats

- `swm1…` — Mainnet, shielded. Unified shielded address. The default in SWARM Wallet.
- `s1…` — Mainnet, transparent. Transparent pay-to-public-key-hash address.
- `s3…` — Mainnet, transparent (script). Pay-to-script-hash, used by the three fund addresses and by mining payouts.
- `swarm1…` — Testnet, shielded. The public testnet keeps its own prefix. Testnet coins have no value.

## Apps

- SWARM Wallet holds, sends and receives SWM, shielded or transparent. Published for Windows, macOS and Linux; also as a hosted web wallet at wallet.swarm.green, held by the SWARM server. Download page: https://swarm.green/ecosystem/wallet
- SWARM Messenger is end-to-end encrypted messaging between SWARM wallets, with payments inside the chat. Published for Windows, macOS and Linux. Download page: https://swarm.green/ecosystem/messenger
- SWARM Browser is a web browser with the SWARM wallet built in. Published for Windows. Download page: https://swarm.green/ecosystem/browser
- Every file and its SHA-256 checksum: https://swarm.green/ecosystem

## Questions and answers

### Is SWARM a privacy coin?

Yes. SWARM is a cryptocurrency whose payments can be shielded: sender, receiver and amount stay encrypted on-chain, using zero-knowledge proofs. It runs on its own proof-of-work blockchain, and its ticker is SWM.

### When did SWARM launch?

SWARM mainnet has been live since 2 October 2026, 15:42 UTC. Its genesis block holds no spendable coins. Until 31 October 2026, 15:42 UTC only the project's own machines can mine: in those 29 days about 33,408 blocks are produced, about 208,800 SWM (80% to the project's mining wallet, 20% to the three funds), about 0.99% of the cap. From then until 1 November 2026, 15:42 UTC the people on the waiting list can mine too; from that moment mining is open to everyone and the node software will be published on this site. Why: the infrastructure around the coin, liquidity pools included, needs coins before public mining begins; the aim is an orderly, predictable start.

### How many SWM will there be?

At most 20,999,987.3152 SWM. Each block pays 6.25 SWM, and the reward halves every 1,680,000 blocks, about every 4 years.

### Was there a premine?

No. The genesis block holds no spendable coins; every SWM that exists has been mined. There is a closed start. Until 31 October 2026, 15:42 UTC only the project's own machines can mine: in those 29 days about 33,408 blocks are produced, about 208,800 SWM (80% to the project's mining wallet, 20% to the three funds), about 0.99% of the cap. From then until 1 November 2026, 15:42 UTC the people on the waiting list can mine too; from that moment mining is open to everyone and the node software will be published on this site. Why: the infrastructure around the coin, liquidity pools included, needs coins before public mining begins; the aim is an orderly, predictable start.

### What does a shielded payment hide?

The sender, the receiver and the amount. The chain records that a valid payment happened, not who paid whom or how much.

### Is every SWARM payment private?

No. Privacy is a choice you make per payment: shielded payments are encrypted on-chain, transparent payments are public, and the wallet tells you which kind you are about to make.

### How do I get SWM?

SWM is created only by mining; you can receive it from someone who already has it. Until 31 October 2026, 15:42 UTC only the project’s own machines mine, and public mining opens on 1 November 2026, 15:42 UTC. SWM has no guaranteed value and can lose value, including all of it.

### Where do block rewards go?

80% Miner · 8% Core Development · 4% Grants & Ecosystem · 8% Community & Development Reserve. The split is fixed in the genesis rules for the whole emission schedule and is visible in every block.

### Who runs SWARM?

A founding team builds the software in the open. Until 31 October 2026, 15:42 UTC the project alone mines; the people on the waiting list follow 24 hours before public mining opens on 1 November 2026, 15:42 UTC, and from then on anyone can run a node and mine, with no account to apply for. There is no admin key, and the rules every node enforces are the same for the founders as for anyone else.

### How do I check that I am on the real SWARM chain?

A chain is identified by its genesis block. SWARM mainnet’s genesis hash is `01b76d8a0f18c502b23ab6605e26296d189aa5770fc4a34155e5c7b250a0eff2`. The [verify page](https://swarm.green/verify) lists the launch facts, the public endpoints and the published addresses.

### Which sources are official?

This site, [@swarm_coin on X](https://x.com/swarm_coin), the email address swarmofficial@atomicmail.io and the code at [github.com/Swarmcoin/swarm-releases](https://github.com/Swarmcoin/swarm-releases). The project will never ask for your recovery words, private keys or a payment.

### Is SWARM live?

Yes. SWARM mainnet has been live since 2 October 2026. Earlier wallet versions (desktop 0.1.0-mainnet.9 and older, Android 0.2.0-mainnet.4) no longer connect to the network; the current version is in the Ecosystem. The genesis hash and the three destination addresses are on the network page, so you can check that the chain you join is the one that was announced. The genesis block holds no spendable coins; every SWM that exists has been mined.

### What is SWM worth?

Whatever people agree it is worth. SWARM does not promise a price. Like any cryptocurrency, SWM can lose value, including all of it. Nothing on this site is financial advice.

### Can I mine SWARM?

Not yet. SWARM is in a closed start: until 31 October 2026, 15:42 UTC only the project’s own machines mine, and for the 24 hours after that the people on the waiting list can mine too. From 1 November 2026, 15:42 UTC mining is open to everyone, and the node software will be published on this site. The proof of work is Equihash 200,9. There is no promise that home computers stay competitive forever. As the network grows and difficulty rises, professional and specialised miners can join — and nothing in the rules keeps anyone out, at either end. Equihash hardware already exists, so that moment can come early. It is a consequence of keeping the rules open, and we say so rather than pretend otherwise.

### Is there a premine or a head start?

The genesis block contains no spendable coins. But the start is not open to everyone. The start is closed for 30 days. Until 31 October 2026, 15:42 UTC only the project’s own machines can mine: in those 29 days about 33,408 blocks are produced, about 208,800 SWM (80% to the project’s mining wallet, 20% to the three funds), about 0.99% of the cap. From then until 1 November 2026, 15:42 UTC the people on the waiting list can mine too; from that moment mining is open to everyone and the node software will be published on this site. Why: an orderly start. Liquidity pools and the infrastructure around the coin need coins before trading and public mining begin, and the project has a responsibility to the people who back it. The coins mined in the closed start are what the project uses for that. The aim is a market that starts stable and predictable rather than chaotic; it is an aim, not a promise about the price. Every coin, those included, has to be mined, and transparent mining rewards mature after 100 blocks before they can be spent.

### How did SWARM mainnet start?

SWARM mainnet has been live since 2 October 2026: its genesis block has the header time 15:41:37 UTC, and block 1 followed at 15:43 UTC. The genesis block contains no spendable coins, so nobody started with a balance. The first 30 days are a closed start: 29 days in which only the project mines, then 24 hours in which the people on the waiting list can mine too; from 1 November 2026, 15:42 UTC mining is open to everyone. The genesis hash and the three destination addresses are published on the verify page, so anyone can check that the chain they are syncing is the one that was announced. The 20% of each block reward that goes to the three project destinations is not a premine and not hidden: it is paid block by block, in public, for the whole life of the chain, and the percentages cannot be changed.

### Who controls the three project destinations?

The project does, under the custody policy published with the launch manifest: keys generated offline, held on separate devices under a threshold policy, with the spending and recovery procedure rehearsed before the addresses were fixed into the rules. It is custody of the project’s share, not a governance vote: nothing can change the percentages.

### How private is it?

Privacy is a choice you make per payment. Shielded transactions keep sender, receiver and amount encrypted on-chain, using zero-knowledge proofs. Transparent transactions do not, and the wallet tells you which kind you are about to make. Shielding protects what is written to the chain. It does not protect everything about how you use the network — for example, your own network connection is a separate matter.

### What is coming after the coin?

SWARM Market, an online marketplace where you pay merchants in SWM; a privacy browser with the wallet built in; and private, end-to-end encrypted messaging with payments inside the conversation. In that order, each when it is finished and reviewed. A first pre-release of SWARM Browser for Windows is already in the Ecosystem. The roadmap has the detail.

### How do I reach the project?

Write to swarmofficial@atomicmail.io or follow @swarm_coin on X. Together with this site and our GitHub, those are the only official channels. Anything else claiming to be SWARM is not us. We will never ask for your recovery words, private keys or a payment — not by email, not on X, not anywhere.
